topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session and outlines the learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor virology revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays developed to detect cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer mutations and demonstrate how oncogenes and tumor suppressors alter cell cycle checkpoints and cellular phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosome instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary cancer syndromes, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the stepwise accumulation of mutations during tumor development and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this progression.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by recommending further reading and previewing the subsequent session.
